The Northstar is our most repaired product by a wide margin, which is a function of how
many we sell and of how it is used, not of any weakness. Nearly every Northstar fault is one

Tools for the Northstar bench: 11 mm and 13 mm open-ended wrenches, the generator

Generator tube replacement
The generator (part G-GEN2) is the tube that runs up through the burner and carries fuel
from the tank to the mantles. Signs of a bad generator are a weak yellow flame that will not
steady, pulsing light, and a tank that holds pressure but will not deliver it. The part is
$13.00, so a typical generator replacement on a yellow tag comes to $38.00 with the bench

1. Confirm the tank is drained and depressurised. Open the filler cap slowly over the tray.
2. Lift off the ventilator and the globe (part G-ND2). Set the globe on the padded shelf,

3. Turn the control valve to the fully open position so the cleaning needle is clear of the

4. Loosen the generator nut at the base of the burner with the 11 mm wrench, then the
fitting at the valve body with the generator wrench. Draw the old generator straight up
and out.
5. Fit the new G-GEN2 with the tip toward the burner. Start both fittings by hand.
6. Tighten the valve body fitting hand-tight plus a quarter turn. Never more than 2.5
N·m. Check with the torque driver if you are new to this; the fitting is brass and strips
easily.
7. Tighten the generator nut the same way.
8. Pressurise with 20 strokes of the pump, no fuel in the tank, and soap-test both fittings.
Any bubbles, back off and reseat. Do not tighten further.
9. Fill with Clearburn white gas, fit the mantles, light under the hood and run the 30-

[4] faq.md > Can I burn kerosene in the Northstar?
### Can I burn kerosene in the Northstar?

No. The Northstar Dual-Fuel burns Clearburn white gas or unleaded gasoline only. Kerosene or
lamp oil will clog its generator in a single evening and the damage is not covered by warranty.

[5] fuel-safety.md > Approved fuels by product
## Approved fuels by product

Each fuel lantern is designed for a particular fuel, and the fuels are not interchangeable.
Using the wrong fuel is the most common cause of damage we see at the Repair Center, and
damage from an unapproved fuel is not covered by the warranty.

| Product | Approved fuel | Never use |
|---|---|---|
| Northstar Dual-Fuel (LS-ND2) | Clearburn white gas or unleaded gasoline | Kerosene, lamp oil |
| Hagerstown Kerosene Lantern (LS-HK12) | K-1 kerosene or Clearburn lamp oil | White gas, gasoline |
| Heritage No. 7 Brass Oil Lamp (LS-H7) | Clearburn lamp oil only | Kerosene, white gas |

The Northstar is called dual-fuel because it burns either Clearburn white gas or ordinary
unleaded gasoline from the pump. White gas burns cleaner and keeps the generator clear for
longer; unleaded is a fallback for when you cannot get white gas, not an everyday fuel. It must
never be fed kerosene. Kerosene will not vaporise in the Northstar's generator; it varnishes the
tube and sticks the check valve, and the lantern will need a paid repair.
